His hundreds of responsa address the commercial, agricultural, family and communal realities of the Ottoman Jewish world. קרית ספר systematically identifies the biblical or rabbinic basis of the laws in Maimonides’ משנה תורה, while בית אלהים treats prayer, repentance and fundamental beliefs. His legal rulings are particularly important for the renewed agricultural settlement of the Land of Israel. Conflicting modern reference traditions date him 1500–1580 or 1505–1585; this record uses the Encyclopaedia Judaica chronology.
title: המבי״ט; פוסק ומנהיג חכמי צפת

name: ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ
bio: ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ (c.1505–1584) was an Ottoman Sephardi kabbalist, biblical commentator and liturgical poet. Born probably in Salonica to a family descended from Spanish exiles, he studied under ר׳ יוסף טאיטאצאק. In 1529, around his marriage, he completed מנות הלוי, a commentary on Esther presented as a wedding gift. Before emigrating to the Land of Israel he taught and wrote in Adrianople, and encountered ר׳ יוסף קארו in the Balkan scholarly network. By about 1535 he had settled in Safed, where he became a formative member of its mystical circle. His student and brother-in-law ר׳ משה קורדובירו became a leading systematic kabbalist. Alkabetz’s enduring contribution is לכה דודי, whose acrostic spells שלמה הלוי and which expresses the Safed practice of welcoming the Sabbath Bride outdoors. His writings include commentaries on Esther, Song of Songs and Ruth and a kabbalistic commentary on the Passover Haggadah.
title: מקובל ופייטן; מחבר לכה דודי

name: ר׳ שמואל בן משה די מדינה
bio: ר׳ שמואל בן משה די מדינה (1506–1589), known as מהרשד״ם, was among the leading Sephardi halakhic authorities of the Ottoman Empire. He was born and spent nearly all his life in Salonika, the great post-expulsion centre of Iberian Jewish learning. He studied under ר׳ יוסף טאיטאצאק and ר׳ לוי בן חביב, then headed an important academy supported by the philanthropist Donna Gracia Mendes. His pupils included ר׳ אברהם די בוטון, author of לחם משנה, and other major scholars who carried Salonikan learning throughout the eastern Mediterranean. Communities from the Balkans, Anatolia and Italy sent him difficult questions, especially in commercial law, communal jurisdiction, marriage and inheritance. His responsa preserve unusually rich evidence about merchants, congregations and the legal pluralism of the Ottoman Jewish world. He was also involved in major disputes of his age, including disagreement with ר׳ יוסף קארו on questions of authority and law. Apart from a communal mission to Constantinople, his securely documented career remained centred in Salonika. His responsa, sermons and talmudic novellae established him as a foundational posek for later Sephardi jurisprudence.
title: מהרשד״ם; פוסק וראש ישיבה בסלוניקי
aliases: ר׳ שמואל בן משה די מדינה

name: ר׳ משה אלשיך
bio: ר׳ משה אלשיך (1508–1593), known as האלשיך הקדוש, was one of sixteenth-century Safed’s foremost preachers, biblical commentators and halakhic authorities. Born in Adrianople, he studied in Salonika under ר׳ יוסף טאיטאצאק and ר׳ יוסף קארו. He settled in Safed around 1535, served on its rabbinical court, led academies and received the renewed semikhah from ר׳ יוסף קארו. His pupils included ר׳ חיים ויטאל and ר׳ יום טוב צהלון. The Alshich’s celebrated biblical commentaries grew from weekly sermons: they combine close textual questions with midrash, ethics and religious philosophy, while generally avoiding overtly technical kabbalah. His Torah commentary, תורת משה, became so influential that it is commonly called simply “the Alshich.” Around 1590, during Safed’s economic decline, he travelled as a communal emissary through Syria and Ottoman lands, perhaps reaching Persia. A Damascus court document proves that he was still active in 1593. Sources disagree whether he died that year or closer to 1600 and whether his last days were in Damascus or Safed; this record follows the standard 1593 chronology and does not turn later tradition into certainty.
title: האלשיך הקדוש; פרשן, דרשן ופוסק בצפת

name: ר׳ שלום שכנא מלובלין
bio: ר׳ שלום שכנא בן יוסף (c.1510–1558), known as ר׳ שלום שכנא מלובלין, was a foundational teacher of early Polish Talmudic scholarship. Born into a prominent Lublin family, he studied under ר׳ יעקב פולק and inherited his teacher’s dialectical method of pilpul. By 1528 he was already famous, and students from across Poland and beyond gathered at his Lublin yeshiva. In 1542 a royal appointment recognized him as one of the senior rabbis responsible for Polish Jewish communal affairs. His academy trained a generation that shaped Ashkenazi halakhah, most famously his student and son-in-law ר׳ משה איסרליש; other pupils included ר׳ חיים בן בצלאל. He preferred oral teaching to literary authority and reportedly instructed his son ר׳ ישראל שכנא not to publish his manuscripts, explaining why so little survives under his name. Two responsa concerning betrothal arrangements and a short decision on kiddushin preserve fragments of his rulings. The claim in the former project record that he was born and studied in Kraków was unsupported and has been removed. He lived, taught and died in Lublin in 1558.
title: ראש ישיבת לובלין ומגדולי חכמי פולין

name: ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא
bio: ר׳ שלמה בן יחיאל לוריא (1510–1573), known as the מהרש״ל or רש״ל, was a leading sixteenth-century Ashkenazic halakhist and Talmudist. Born according to the prevailing tradition in Brest-Litovsk, he spent part of his youth with learned relatives in Poznań and studied in Lublin under ר׳ שלום שכנא. He was also associated with the Ostroh scholarly circle and married Lipka, daughter of ר׳ קלונימוס הברקסטן. After rabbinic service in Brest and other Lithuanian communities, he became rabbi and rosh yeshiva in Ostroh around 1550 and moved to Lublin in the mid-1550s. There he created an independent academy and became one of Polish Jewry’s most authoritative decisors. His ים של שלמה reconstructs practical halakhah through close examination of the Talmud, earlier commentators and communal custom; it often resists the compression of law into codes. חכמת שלמה records critical corrections and explanations based on manuscripts and early printed Talmuds, while his responsa illuminate ritual, civil and communal law. He corresponded and disagreed sharply but respectfully with his relative and former fellow student ר׳ משה איסרליש. Later authorities prized both his textual independence and insistence that legal conclusions remain grounded in the sugya. He died in Lublin on 7 November 1573 and was buried in its Old Jewish Cemetery.
title: פוסק, פרשן התלמוד וראש ישיבה בלובלין

name: ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי
bio: ר׳ אליעזר בן אליהו אשכנזי (1512–1585) was a remarkably mobile rabbi, physician and independent biblical exegete. Born into an Ashkenazi family at an uncertain location, he studied in Salonika under ר׳ יוסף טאיטאצאק. From 1538 to 1560 he served as a rabbi in Egypt, probably at Fustat, before political circumstances drove him to Famagusta in Cyprus. His subsequent career carried him through Venice, Prague, Crimea, Cremona, Poznań, Gniezno and Kraków. In Prague his signature headed the regulations of the communal burial society; in Italy and Poland he repeatedly entered vigorous intellectual and halakhic controversy. His rationalist מעשי ה׳ interprets the narrative sections of the Torah and the Passover Haggadah using philosophy, medicine and close textual reasoning. יוסף לקח, his commentary on Esther, was dedicated to ר׳ יוסף נשיא and printed at Cremona. His outlook resisted both scholastic pilpul and uncritical mystical explanation, bringing him into disagreement with figures including the מהר״ל. He completed מעשי ה׳ at Gniezno in 1580 and died in Kraków on 13 December 1585, where his grave survives in the Remuh Cemetery.
title: רב, רופא ופרשן; בעל מעשי ה׳

name: ר׳ בצלאל בן אברהם אשכנזי
bio: ר׳ בצלאל בן אברהם אשכנזי (c.1520–c.1592), known through שיטה מקובצת, was a major Ottoman Talmudist and communal leader. Probably born in Jerusalem or Safed to a family of German origin, he studied with ר׳ ישראל די קוריאל and moved around 1540 to Cairo, where ר׳ דוד אבן זמרא became his principal teacher. After the Radbaz left Egypt, ר׳ בצלאל succeeded him as head of the Egyptian rabbis and led a yeshiva whose scholars included ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי, ר׳ אברהם מונסון, and later ר׳ שלמה עדני. He intervened forcefully in communal government, helping abolish the increasingly arbitrary office of nagid. His great literary project, first called אספת זקנים and later שיטה מקובצת, copied, compared, and arranged Geonic and Rishonic novellae by tractate, preserving texts otherwise lost. The familiar material on Kodashim was shaped from his marginalia by ר׳ שלמה עדני and should not simply be treated as his finished text. By 1587 he had moved to Jerusalem, where Sephardi and Ashkenazi communities accepted his leadership; he negotiated a taxation settlement and strengthened local institutions. He revisited Egypt in 1591 and apparently returned to Jerusalem, dying in the early 1590s. His responsa appeared posthumously at Venice in 1595.
title: בעל שיטה מקובצת — רבה של מצרים וראש חכמי ירושלים

name: ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל
bio: ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל (c.1520–1609), known as המהר״ל מפראג, was a rabbi, communal reformer and one of early modern Judaism’s most original thinkers. Probably born in Poznań to a family with roots in Worms, he served from 1553 to 1573 as Landesrabbiner of Moravia at Nikolsburg, regulating taxation, communal elections, education and limits on luxury. In Prague he founded the Klaus yeshiva, organized Mishnah study and revised the burial society’s statutes. After a period in Poznań, he returned to Prague and eventually became its chief rabbi. In 1592 he received an audience with Emperor Rudolf II; the subject is uncertain, despite later mystical legend. His books joined close rabbinic reading with a comprehensive theology of creation, Torah, exile, redemption and moral character. גור אריה defended and expanded ר׳ שלמה יצחקי’s Torah commentary; דרך חיים, נתיבות עולם, תפארת ישראל, נצח ישראל and באר הגולה became central works of Jewish thought. The famous claim that he created the Prague Golem is a much later literary legend, not a documented episode of his life. He died in Prague and was buried in its Old Jewish Cemetery.
title: המהר״ל מפראג; רב, הוגה וראש ישיבה

name: ר׳ שמואל יהודה קצנלנבוגן
bio: ר׳ שמואל יהודה קצנלנבוגן (1521–1597), known as מהרשי״ק, was a leading Italian rabbi, preacher and halakhist. Born in Padua, he was the son and student of ר׳ מאיר קצנלנבוגן, the מהר״ם מפדובה, and descended through his mother from ר׳ יהודה מינץ. His scholarship and oratorical ability were recognised early, and he collaborated with his father in teaching, responsa and textual work. After his father’s death in 1565 he was chosen as rabbi of Venice, where he headed an important academy and taught numerous pupils. Authorities across Europe—including ר׳ יוסף קארו, the מהרש״ל and ר׳ משה איסרליש—treated him with respect, and several of his responsa survive within their collections. He contributed notes to the 1550 Venice edition of Maimonides’ משנה תורה and composed twelve sermons, printed by a pupil in 1594. His son ר׳ שאול וואהל became the subject of the celebrated Polish “king for a day” legend. ר׳ שמואל יהודה died on 25 March 1597; ר׳ יהודה אריה ממודנה delivered his funeral oration. A reported sculpted bust made by an admiring pupil is not securely identifiable today and is therefore not used as his image.
title: מהרשי״ק; רבה של ונציה ודרשן

name: ר׳ משה קורדובירו
bio: ר׳ משה קורדובירו (1522–1570), universally known as הרמ״ק, was the foremost systematizer of pre-Lurianic Kabbalah in sixteenth-century Safed. His family name points to Iberian origins, but his birthplace is unknown and almost all secure biographical evidence concerns Safed. He studied Talmud and halakhah under ר׳ יוסף קארו, from whom he received semikhah, and began intensive kabbalistic study at age twenty with his brother-in-law ר׳ שלמה הלוי אלקבץ. He served Safed as a dayan and rosh yeshiva while gathering a major mystical school. His students included ר׳ אליהו די וידאש and, briefly at the end of his life, ר׳ יצחק לוריא. פרדס רימונים, completed by age twenty-seven, organized earlier Zoharic and kabbalistic traditions into a coherent speculative system. אילימה רבתי developed that synthesis further, while אור יקר offered a vast running interpretation of the Zohar. תומר דבורה translated his theology into an enduring programme of ethical imitation of the divine attributes. His system remained foundational even after Lurianic Kabbalah reshaped Safed’s mystical language. He died there on 25 June 1570.
title: הרמ״ק; מקובל, דיין וראש ישיבה בצפת

name: ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא
bio: ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא (1526–1587) was an Italian talmudist and historian from a distinguished Portuguese-Sephardi family. Born at Imola, he studied at Ferrara and later lived in Rovigo. The burning of the Talmud and intensifying papal restrictions repeatedly displaced him: he spent time in Salonika, returned to Imola, and after the expulsions ordered under Pius V moved through Pesaro, Ferrara and other Italian centres. Amid this instability he laboured for decades on שלשלת הקבלה, beginning it at Ravenna in 1549 and completing it shortly before his death. Printed in Venice in 1587, the work combines a chain of rabbinic tradition, Jewish chronology, accounts of surrounding nations and discussions of philosophy, science and marvels. Although later historians criticised its chronology and legendary material, it became one of the most widely read early modern Hebrew chronicles and preserves valuable evidence about expulsions and Iberian Jewish memory. Older accounts placed his death at Alexandria in Egypt; modern research considers Alessandria in Piedmont more probable. This record follows the modern 1526–1587 chronology and maps the Italian Alessandria cautiously.
title: תלמודיסט וכרוניקן; בעל שלשלת הקבלה
aliases: ר׳ גדליה בן יוסף אבן יחיא

name: ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה
bio: ר׳ מרדכי בן אברהם יפה (c.1530–1612), known as the לבוש or בעל הלבושים, was a Bohemian-Polish rabbi, halakhist, kabbalist and communal leader. Born in Prague, he studied in Poland under ר׳ שלמה לוריא and ר׳ משה איסרליש and learned Kabbalah from ר׳ מתתיהו דלקרוט. He headed a Prague yeshiva from 1553 until the expulsion of Bohemian Jewry in 1561 forced him to Venice. During roughly a decade in Italy he deepened his study of astronomy, calendar science, philosophy and Kabbalah. Returning to Poland-Lithuania, he held rabbinates in Grodno, Kremenets and Lublin and participated in the Council of the Lands. He returned as rabbi of Prague in 1592 and later exchanged positions with ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל, becoming chief rabbi of Poznań in 1599. His ten-part לבוש מלכות sought a middle course between the expansive בית יוסף and the compressed שולחן ערוך, explaining legal reasoning while preserving Ashkenazic practice. Its first sections, לבוש התכלת and לבוש החור, appeared in Lublin in 1590; later “garments” addressed the remaining divisions of law, biblical interpretation, ר׳ שלמה יצחקי, philosophy, astronomy and Kabbalah. The work became a foundational halakhic reference and generated an extensive supercommentary tradition. He died in Poznań on 7 March 1612.
title: פוסק, מקובל ורב פראג ופוזנא

name: ר׳ משה איסרליש
bio: ר׳ משה בן ישראל איסרליש (c.1530–1572), the רמ״א, was Kraków’s leading rabbi and the decisive codifier of Ashkenazi practice in early modern Europe. Born into a wealthy communal family, he studied in Lublin under ר׳ שלום שכנא and returned to Kraków while still young to serve on its rabbinical court and lead a major yeshiva. His דרכי משה supplements the בית יוסף of ר׳ יוסף קארו with Ashkenazi authorities and customs. When שולחן ערוך appeared, his concise glosses, known as המפה, integrated those traditions into the code; their inclusion made the work broadly authoritative across both Sephardi and Ashkenazi communities. His scholarship extended beyond practical halakhah to philosophy, Kabbalah, biblical interpretation, custom, and astronomy. תורת חטאת systematised dietary and ritual law, while תורת העולה interpreted the Temple and sacrifices philosophically and kabbalistically. His independent responsa document the legal, economic, and communal life of sixteenth-century Polish Jewry. He corresponded with ר׳ יוסף קארו and debated leading contemporaries including ר׳ שלמה לוריא. He died in Kraków on 18 Iyar 5332 and was buried beside the synagogue founded by his family in Kazimierz; both the Remuh Synagogue and his grave remain major landmarks.
title: הרמ״א — אב״ד קרקוב ופוסק יהדות אשכנז

name: ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי
bio: ר׳ יצחק לוריא אשכנזי (1534–1572), the האר״י הקדוש or אריז״ל, was the formative teacher of Lurianic Kabbalah. Born in Jerusalem to an Ashkenazi father and Sephardi mother, he lost his father while young and was raised in Cairo by his maternal uncle Mordecai Frances. He studied rabbinic law with leading Egyptian scholars, including ר׳ בצלאל אשכנזי, while undertaking extended solitary study of the Zohar near the Nile. After returning to the Land of Israel in 1569, he settled in Safed, where ר׳ משה קורדובירו briefly influenced him before the latter’s death. During only about two years of public teaching, he gathered a circle known as the גורי האר״י, with ר׳ חיים ויטאל as principal recorder. His oral system recast Kabbalah around צמצום, שבירת הכלים, תיקון, פרצופים, גלגול, and precise liturgical כוונות. He wrote very little himself; works commonly called “the writings of the Ari,” including עץ חיים and שער הכוונות, were arranged from the notes of ר׳ חיים ויטאל and later transmitters and must not be mistaken for autograph books. The system transformed Sephardi devotion, Jewish liturgy, messianism, and later Hasidism. He died in Safed during an epidemic on 5 Av 5332 and was buried in the city’s ancient cemetery.
title: האר״י הקדוש — מייסד הקבלה הלוריאנית

name: ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז
bio: ר׳ דוד בן שלמה גנז (1541–1613), known by his chronicle צמח דוד, was a pioneering Jewish historian, mathematician and astronomer of Renaissance Prague. Born in Lippstadt, Westphalia, he studied in Bonn and Frankfurt before joining the Kraków academy of ר׳ משה איסרליש. In 1564 he moved to Prague, where he learned from ר׳ סיני בן בצלאל and the מהר״ל. A period in Nordheim introduced him to Euclidean mathematics. Back in Prague he engaged both Jewish learning and the new astronomy of the Rudolfine court, working in the intellectual orbit of Tycho Brahe and Johannes Kepler. צמח דוד, first printed in Prague in 1592, combines Jewish chronology with a separate history of the nations and became a landmark of early modern Hebrew historiography. His astronomical work מגן דוד was announced in 1612; its fuller text appeared posthumously as נחמד ונעים. Gans treated mathematics and astronomy as legitimate branches of divine wisdom and helped translate contemporary scientific knowledge into Hebrew. He died in Prague in 1613 and was buried in the Old Jewish Cemetery, where his tombstone bears a goose—an emblematic play on the German word Gans.
title: היסטוריון, מתמטיקאי ואסטרונום יהודי

name: ר׳ חיים ויטאל
bio: ר׳ חיים ויטאל (1542–1620), known by the acronym מהרח״ו and also as Chaim Vital Calabrese, was the principal recorder and transmitter of the teachings of ר׳ יצחק לוריא, the האר״י. Born in Safed to the scribe Joseph Vital Calabrese, whose family originated in Calabria, he studied revealed Torah under ר׳ משה אלשיך and Kabbalah in the intellectual world shaped by ר׳ משה קורדובירו. When the האר״י settled in Safed in 1570, ר׳ חיים became his leading disciple and recorded the new Lurianic system during the master's final two years. After 1572 he organized a circle of disciples and asserted authority over the transmission of those teachings, although other disciples circulated competing recensions. His movements took him through Egypt, Ein al-Zeitun, Jerusalem, Safed and finally Damascus, where he taught Kabbalah and led a scholarly circle. His writings include his own ethical-mystical שערי קדושה, biblical commentary עץ הדעת טוב and autobiographical dream diary ספר החזיונות, alongside the enormous record of the האר״י's teachings later arranged by his son ר׳ שמואל ויטאל as שמונה שערים. Familiar titles such as עץ חיים and שער הגלגולים emerged through several manuscript recensions and later editors, so their attribution requires bibliographic caution. His record became the principal channel through which Lurianic Kabbalah transformed Sephardi spirituality, European Kabbalah, liturgy and later Hasidism.
title: מהרח״ו, תלמידו המובהק של האר״י ועורך קבלת האר״י

name: ר׳ אברהם די בוטון
bio: ר׳ אברהם בן משה די בוטון (c.1545–c.1605), often called the לחם משנה, was an Ottoman Sephardi halakhist and one of the most enduring commentators on משנה תורה. Born into a Salonikan rabbinic family, he studied in the yeshiva of ר׳ שמואל די מדינה alongside ר׳ מרדכי קלעי. He later served the Apulian congregation of Salonika as rabbi and led a Talmudic academy. His commentary לחם משנה traces difficult rulings of ר׳ משה בן מימון to their Talmudic sources, compares them with later authorities, and frequently clarifies points left unresolved by כסף משנה. After כסף משנה appeared in 1575, he revised his treatment to distinguish his own observations and record agreement or disagreement. His responsa, gathered as לחם רב, illuminate the legal and commercial life of the Sephardi diaspora. Evidence places him chiefly in Salonika, with late visits or residence reported in the Land of Israel and Constantinople. He died during a plague sometime between 1603 and 1609. לחם משנה was first printed at Venice in 1604 and became a standard page-side commentary in editions of משנה תורה.
title: בעל לחם משנה — פוסק וראש ישיבה בסלוניקי

name: ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו
bio: ר׳ מנחם עזריה מפאנו (1548–1620), known as הרמ״ע מפאנו, was the leading Italian exponent of Cordoverian Kabbalah and a major halakhic authority. Born into a wealthy Italian family, probably at Fano, he studied with ר׳ ישמעאל חנינא of Valmontone in Ferrara. ר׳ משה קורדובירו sent him פרדס רמונים, and after the author’s death he sought to acquire and preserve his manuscripts. He later learned Lurianic Kabbalah from ר׳ ישראל סרוג without abandoning the Ramak’s system. Active in Ferrara, Venice, Reggio and Mantua, he combined scholarship with patronage: he helped finance publication of קארו’s כסף משנה and Cordovero’s פרדס רמונים and aided victims of the 1570 Ferrara earthquake. His 130 responsa demonstrate broad authority in Italian communal and ritual law. His many kabbalistic treatises, later grouped as עשרה מאמרות, shaped the reception of Safed Kabbalah in Europe; אלפסי זוטא abridged and annotated the Rif. He eventually served the Mantua community and died there on 4 Av 5380 (1620). He should not be confused with ר׳ משה איסרליש, the Polish Rema.
title: הרמ״ע מפאנו; פוסק ומקובל איטלקי

name: ר׳ שלמה אפרים מלונטשיץ
bio: ר׳ שלמה אפרים בן ר׳ אהרן מלונטשיץ (c. 1550–1619), known as the בעל כלי יקר, was one of the leading Polish-Jewish preachers, biblical commentators and communal rabbis of the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries. Born in Łęczyca—rendered Luntschitz in Jewish sources—he was originally named אפרים; שלמה was added during a life-threatening illness, as he records in his introduction to כלי יקר. He studied under ר׳ שלמה לוריא (מהרש״ל) in Lublin and later headed a yeshiva in Lviv. His early publications established him as a moralist and master preacher: עיר גיבורים appeared in 1580, עוללות אפרים in 1590 and אורח לחיים in 1595. His best-known work, כלי יקר, was first printed in Lublin in 1602. It combines close biblical reading, midrash, moral psychology and public rebuke, frequently criticizing social inequality, ostentation, corrupt leadership and sterile methods of study. In 1604 he was appointed rabbi and prominent preacher in Prague, serving the community during the generation of ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל (מהר״ל). His Prague writings included שפתי דעת and עמודי שש. He also composed penitential poems after violence struck Prague in 1611. His students and intellectual circle helped transmit Polish Torah learning into Bohemia; later tradition counts figures such as ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר among those influenced by him. He died in Prague in 1619 and was buried in its Old Jewish Cemetery. כלי יקר remains widely printed in editions of the Torah and מקראות גדולות.
title: בעל כלי יקר
aliases: ר׳ שלמה אפרים בן אהרן לונטשיץ

name: ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס
bio: ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס (1555–1631), known by the acronym מהרש״א, was one of the most influential commentators on the Babylonian Talmud. Born into a distinguished rabbinic family, he married the daughter of ר׳ משה אשכנזי. His mother-in-law Edel supported a large yeshiva that he directed in Poznań from about 1585 until her death; in gratitude he adopted the family designation Eidels. In 1590 he joined leading rabbis at Lublin in opposing the purchase of rabbinic offices. After the Poznań academy closed, he served as rabbi of Chełm from 1610, became rabbi and rosh yeshiva of Lublin in 1614, then served Tykocin and finally Ostroh. His חידושי הלכות closely analyze the Talmud together with the commentaries of ר׳ שלמה יצחקי and the Tosafists, while חידושי אגדות treat narrative passages as intellectually and ethically serious components of the same discourse. He regretted their separate publication and urged later printers to integrate them, as standard Talmud editions eventually did. His learning combined legal analysis, biblical interpretation, philosophy and an unusually sustained engagement with aggadah. He was also remembered for supporting students and travelers. He died in Ostroh on 30 November 1631, and his tomb remains associated with the city’s historic Jewish cemetery.
title: פרשן התלמוד, פוסק וראש ישיבה

name: ר׳ יהושע פלק כ״ץ
bio: ר׳ יהושע פלק כ״ץ (1555–1614), commonly known as הסמ״ע and as the author of דרישה ופרישה, was one of the formative halakhists of early modern Poland. He studied under his relative ר׳ משה איסרליש and under ר׳ שלמה לוריא, absorbing both the Kraków codificatory tradition and the Maharshal’s close talmudic criticism. After marriage he settled in Lemberg, where the communal leader Joseph Edels supported the yeshiva he headed. His בית ישראל commentary on the ארבעה טורים was divided in print into פרישה, explaining the rulings, and דרישה, probing their talmudic foundations and disagreements. His ספר מאירת עינים—whose initials form סמ״ע—became a standard commentary on the חושן משפט section of the שולחן ערוך. Falk also played a public role in the Council of Four Lands; enactments he proposed were adopted at Kremenets in 1607. A controversial get issued at Vienna in 1611 produced a major debate with the מהר״ם מלובלין and the לבוש, illustrating both his independence and authority. He died in Lemberg in 1614.
title: הסמ״ע; בעל דרישה ופרישה

name: ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה מלובלין
bio: ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה (1558–1616), the מהר״ם מלובלין, was one of the outstanding Polish Talmudists and halakhic decisors of the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries. Born in Lublin to a learned family, he studied chiefly under his father-in-law, ר׳ יצחק הכהן שפירא of Kraków. Still in his twenties he headed the Lublin yeshiva, and in 1587 he was appointed dayan and head of the yeshiva in Kraków. From about 1595 until 1613 he served as rabbi of Lemberg, where his responsa record communal, commercial and family-law questions and a celebrated disagreement with ר׳ יהושע פלק כץ. He then returned to Lublin as rabbi and rosh yeshiva, dying there in 1616. His חידושי הלכות, conventionally known as מאיר עיני חכמים, became a standard aid to the Tosafot and to close analysis of the Babylonian Talmud; his responsa illuminate the social and economic life of early modern Polish Jewry. His pupils included ר׳ נתן נטע שפירא, and his analytical method helped shape the great Polish yeshiva tradition that followed.
title: מהר״ם מלובלין; ראש ישיבה ופוסק

name: ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ
bio: ר׳ ישעיהו הלוי הורוביץ (1558–traditionally 1630), universally known as the השל״ה הקדוש after his work שני לוחות הברית, was an Ashkenazic rabbi, communal judge, halakhist and kabbalist. Born in Prague to ר׳ אברהם הלוי הורוביץ, he was educated in Poland and studied with leading scholars including ר׳ שלמה לוריא’s and ר׳ משה איסרליש’s intellectual successors. He attended the Council of Four Lands and held rabbinic offices in Dubno, Ostroh, Posen and Frankfurt am Main. Expelled from Frankfurt during the Fettmilch uprising, he returned to Prague and became a senior communal rabbi. After his wife’s death he left Europe in 1621, travelled through the Ottoman Empire and settled in Jerusalem, where he promoted rigorous observance of the sabbatical year and completed major portions of שני לוחות הברית. In 1625 the Jerusalem pasha imprisoned leading Jews, including the של״ה, for ransom. After release he left Jerusalem, passed through Safed and settled in Tiberias. His encyclopedic שני לוחות הברית integrates law, ethics, ritual and Kabbalah and profoundly shaped later Ashkenazic piety and Hasidism. Traditional chronology places his death in Tiberias in 1630, though recent textual scholarship argues for late 1625 or early 1626. He was buried near the tomb associated with ר׳ משה בן מימון.
title: השל״ה הקדוש; בעל שני לוחות הברית

name: ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון
bio: ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון (1559–1620), known as מהריט״ץ, was a distinguished Safed halakhist of the generation after ר׳ יוסף קארו. His family was of Spanish origin, although neither his birthplace nor the date of its migration is known. In Safed he studied under ר׳ משה מטראני and ר׳ משה אלשיך, from whom he received semikhah. Already at twenty-five, ר׳ שמואל יפה of Constantinople asked him to decide a difficult legal problem, evidence of his early standing. His responsa address ritual, commercial, family and communal disputes throughout the Ottoman world. He corresponded and disagreed with leading contemporaries, notably ר׳ משה גלאנטי. In a Jerusalem dispute between Sephardi and Ashkenazi congregations he ruled for the Ashkenazim, and he did not hesitate to question individual rulings of ר׳ יוסף קארו. He travelled on communal business to Egypt and Constantinople, but Safed remained the centre of his scholarly identity. His works include לקח טוב on Esther, מגן אבות on Avot, talmudic novellae and a large responsa corpus. Encyclopaedia Judaica dates his death to 1619/20; the later 1638 date is not used here.
title: מהריט״ץ; פוסק מחכמי צפת
aliases: ר׳ יום טוב בן משה צהלון

name: ר׳ יואל בן שמואל סירקיש
bio: ר׳ יואל בן שמואל סירקיש (1561–1640), known as the ב״ח from בית חדש, was one of the leading halakhic authorities of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth. Born in Lublin, he studied first with ר׳ נפתלי צבי הירש שור, a disciple of ר׳ משה איסרליש, and then at Brest under ר׳ פייבוש. He served a succession of communities—including Pruzhany, Łuków, Lublin, Medzhybizh, Belz, Szydłów, and Brest—before becoming av bet din and head of the yeshiva in Kraków in 1619. His בית חדש on ארבעה טורים traces rulings back through Talmud, Geonim, Rif, Tosafists, and Rosh, frequently corrects texts, and resists deciding law from abbreviated codes without examining their sources. Published at Kraków from 1631 to 1639, it became inseparable from advanced study of the Tur. His responsa address ritual, civil, commercial, and communal problems and provide valuable evidence for early-seventeenth-century Polish Jewish life. He combined legal independence with respect for Kabbalah while rejecting mystical customs that contradicted halakhah. His students included ר׳ גרשון אשכנזי and ר׳ מנחם מנדל קרוכמל; his son-in-law ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל became known as the ט״ז. He died in Kraków on 14 March 1640 and was buried in the Remuh Cemetery.
title: הב״ח — אב בית דין קרקוב ופוסק

name: ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו
bio: ר׳ יאשיהו בן יוסף פינטו (1565–1648), מחכמי סוריה וארץ ישראל, נולד בדמשק למשפחה אמידה של יוצאי ספרד. הוא למד תלמוד וקבלה, ונעשה תלמידו המובהק של ר׳ יעקב אבולעפיה, שהעניק לו סמיכה מן השרשרת שחידש ר׳ יעקב בירב. מרכז חייו היה בדמשק, אך הוא שהה גם בחלב ובירושלים. בשנת 1625 ניסה להשתקע בצפת; מות בנו הצעיר ר׳ יוסף בשנה שלאחר מכן הביאו לשוב לדמשק, ושם ירש את הנהגת הקהילה לאחר פטירת ר׳ חיים ויטאל. הוא נודע כדרשן וכפרשן, ובייחוד בפירושו מאור עינים לאגדות עין יעקב, שבעקבותיו כונה הרי״ף או ריא״ף — כינוי שאין לבלבל בינו ובין ר׳ יצחק אלפסי. כתביו משלבים פרשנות מקרא, דרוש ומוסר, וחלקם נדפסו עוד בחייו וחלקם זמן רב לאחר מותו. הפרטים הכרונולוגיים של ביקוריו בחלב ובירושלים אינם תמיד אחידים במקורות, ולכן המפה מציגה רק את התחנות הנתמכות במפורש ומסמנת תאריכים מקורבים. חיפושים בוויקיפדיות, בוויקישיתוף, בספרייה הלאומית ובמאגרי מורשת לא העלו דיוקן מאומת שלו.
title: רבה של דמשק; בעל הרי״ף על עין יעקב

name: ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר
bio: ר׳ יום טוב ליפמן הלר (1579–1654), known through his classic Mishnah commentary תוספות יום טוב, was a leading rabbi of Prague, Vienna and Poland. Born at Wallerstein after his father’s death, he was raised by his grandfather and studied at Friedberg before joining the Prague academy of ר׳ יהודה ליווא בן בצלאל, the Maharal. At eighteen he became a dayan in Prague. His תוספות יום טוב, printed there in parts from 1614 to 1617, expanded the commentary of ר׳ עובדיה מברטנורא through close Talmudic and halakhic analysis. After brief service at Mikulov he became av bet din of Vienna and then chief rabbi of Prague. In 1629 hostile accusations concerning taxation and allegedly anti-Christian passages led to imprisonment in Vienna, a heavy fine and removal from office; he later memorialized the ordeal in מגילת איבה. Moving to Poland in 1631, he served communities including Nemyriv and Volodymyr before becoming rabbi of Kraków, where he revised his Mishnah commentary and headed the yeshiva. He also wrote מעדני מלך and לחם חמודות on the halakhic work of ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל. His career links the Maharal’s Prague with the great Polish Torah centers before and during the 1648 upheavals.
title: בעל תוספות יום טוב; אב״ד פראג וקראקא
aliases: גרשון שאול יום טוב ליפמן הלר

name: ר׳ נתן נטע שפירא
bio: ר׳ נתן נטע בן שלמה שפירא (c.1585–1633), known as the מגלה עמוקות, was a major early-modern Polish kabbalist, preacher, dayan and rosh yeshiva. Born in Kazimierz beside Kraków into a distinguished rabbinic family, he was named for his grandfather, the Grodno rabbi who wrote מבוא שערים and אמרי שפר. He probably studied in the intellectual circle of ר׳ מאיר בן גדליה מלובלין and became renowned for combining exacting rabbinic learning with a numerically and symbolically intricate Kabbalah influenced by Lurianic traditions. In 1617 he succeeded to leadership of the principal Talmudic academy in Kazimierz and served on the rabbinical court. His מגלה עמוקות על ואתחנן offered 252 interpretations—רנ״ב אופנים—of the prayer of משה רבנו in Deuteronomy 3:23–25. Published by his son at Kraków in 1637, four years after the author’s death, it became a classic of Ashkenazic Kabbalah. Other Torah writings circulated in manuscript and appeared much later. He died in Kraków in 1633 and is buried in the Remuh Cemetery, where his tombstone identifies him as a revered teacher and revealer of hidden meanings.
title: בעל מגלה עמוקות; מקובל וראש ישיבה בקראקא

name: ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל
bio: ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל (בקירוב 1586–1667), הנודע בכינוי הט״ז על שם חיבורו טורי זהב, היה מן הפוסקים המרכזיים של יהדות פולין במאה השבע־עשרה. הוא נולד בלודמיר שבווהלין, למד בישיבות פולין, ונשא את בתו של ר׳ יואל סירקיש, הב״ח, שהיה גם רבו ומקור השפעה מרכזי על דרכו ההלכתית. לאחר תקופות רבנות בפוטליץ ובפוזנן נתמנה לרב ולאב בית דין באוסטרוה, ושם השלים את פירושו ליורה דעה. החיבור נדפס בלובלין בשנת 1646 והעמיד אותו במרכז הדיון ההלכתי בן זמנו. גזרות ת״ח–ת״ט ומלחמות אמצע המאה אילצו אותו לעקור ממקומו; לאחר נדודים הגיע ללבוב, ובה כיהן ברבנות עד פטירתו. חלקים נוספים של טורי זהב, על אורח חיים, אבן העזר וחושן משפט, נדפסו בחייו ולאחריו ונקבעו בדפוסי השולחן ערוך. מחלוקותיו עם ר׳ שבתי הכהן, הש״ך, הן נדבך יסודי בספרות הפסיקה האשכנזית. מקום הולדתו ונתיב בריחתו תוקנו כאן על פי המקורות: המסורת המחקרית מצביעה על לודמיר, ולא על קרקוב, ואין די ראיות למפות תחנות־פליטות מדויקות שלא תועדו.
title: בעל הט״ז; פוסק ורב בלבוב

name: ר׳ משה רבקש
bio: ר׳ משה בן נפתלי הירש רבקש (c.1595–1671), known as the באר הגולה, was a Lithuanian halakhist whose source-notes became a standard component of printed editions of the שולחן ערוך. His precise birthplace is disputed, but he spent most of his adult life in Vilna and became one of the city’s notable scholars. When Muscovite and Cossack forces captured Vilna in 1655, he fled west with other scholars, including ר׳ שבתי הכהן and ר׳ אהרן שמואל קוידנובר. Blocked near the Prussian frontier by the Swedish war, he eventually reached Amsterdam by sea. There the Portuguese community, aided by ר׳ שאול לוי מורטירה and ר׳ יצחק אבוהב דה פונסקה, enabled him to remain and work on a major Amsterdam edition of the שולחן ערוך. His באר הגולה supplied concise references to the Talmudic and early halakhic sources behind the code and clarified apparent conflicts among rulings. Because the annotations were printed alongside the code from the Amsterdam edition onward, they became part of the everyday apparatus through which generations studied Jewish law. After conditions permitted, he returned to Vilna, where he died around 1671. He was an ancestor of ר׳ אליהו מווילנה.
title: בעל באר הגולה; מחכמי וילנה

name: ר׳ חיים בנבנישתי
bio: ר׳ חיים בנבנישתי (1603–1673), known as the כנסת הגדולה, was a pre-eminent Ottoman halakhist whose compilations became indispensable guides to post–שולחן ערוך jurisprudence. Born in Constantinople into the distinguished Benveniste family, he studied under ר׳ יוסף מטראני and was the brother of ר׳ יהושע בנבנישתי. In 1644 he received a rabbinic appointment at Tire near İzmir, and in 1658 became one of İzmir’s leading rabbis. His כנסת הגדולה and שיירי כנסת הגדולה systematically gathered responsa and rulings omitted from or written after the בית יוסף, organizing an immense body of Sephardic and Ashkenazic precedent around the ארבעה טורים and שולחן ערוך. Portions on אורח חיים and חושן משפט appeared during his lifetime; other sections were printed posthumously. During the Sabbatean crisis he initially accepted שבתאי צבי’s claims under intense local conditions but withdrew after the apostasy and opposed the movement’s adherents. Alongside his codes he wrote בעי חיי, a substantial responsa collection, and Talmudic novellae. His method of recording divergent customs and authorities preserved otherwise inaccessible legal material, and later decisors—especially ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי—treated consultation of כנסת הגדולה as essential before issuing a ruling. He died and was buried in İzmir in 1673.
title: בעל כנסת הגדולה; מרבני איזמיר

name: ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל
bio: ר׳ מנשה בן ישראל (1604–1657), born Manoel Dias Soeiro to a Portuguese New Christian family, became an Amsterdam rabbi, preacher, author, printer and diplomat. His birthplace is disputed between Lisbon and La Rochelle. After the family reached Amsterdam around 1613 and openly returned to Judaism, he studied under ר׳ יצחק עוזיאל and emerged as an unusually multilingual scholar. He began preaching while still young and in 1626 established the first enduring Hebrew press in Amsterdam, publishing Hebrew, Spanish, Portuguese and Latin works. His El Conciliador sought to reconcile apparent biblical contradictions and brought him into correspondence with Christian humanists, scholars and artists, including Rembrandt. Mikveh Israel (The Hope of Israel, 1650) connected reports about Indigenous Americans with the Ten Lost Tribes and helped frame his campaign for Jewish resettlement in England. In 1655 he travelled to London, submitted the Humble Addresses to Oliver Cromwell and participated in the debate surrounding the Whitehall Conference. No formal readmission decree resulted, but Jews were thereafter able to worship and organize more openly. He defended them in Vindiciae Judaeorum (1656). Returning after his son Samuel’s death, he died at Middelburg on 20 November 1657 and was buried at Beth Haim, Ouderkerk aan de Amstel.
title: רב, דרשן, מדפיס ודיפלומט

name: ר׳ יעקב ששפורטש
bio: ר׳ יעקב בן אהרן ששפורטש (1610–1698) was an Algerian-born Sephardi rabbi, diplomat and one of the most determined opponents of the Sabbatean movement. Born and educated in Spanish-held Oran, he joined the Tlemcen rabbinical court while young and later served Jewish communities in Tlemcen, Marrakesh, Fez and Salé. Conflict with Moroccan authorities led to imprisonment and flight to Amsterdam. He later undertook a diplomatic mission to Spain for the Moroccan ruler and in 1664 accepted leadership of London’s newly re-established Portuguese congregation. The Great Plague drove him to Hamburg in 1665, precisely as the claims of שבתאי צבי swept Jewish communities. From Hamburg he conducted an international correspondence challenging reports of miracles, demanding evidence and resisting communal pressure. Preserved in ציצת נובל צבי, that correspondence is among the most important contemporary records of the Sabbatean crisis. He later headed Keter Torah in Amsterdam, served as dayan and rosh yeshiva in Livorno, returned to lead Ets Haim in Amsterdam, and in 1693 succeeded ר׳ יצחק אבוהב דה פונסקה as rabbi of the Portuguese community. He died in Amsterdam in 1698.
title: חכם, דיין ומתנגד מרכזי לשבתאות

name: ר׳ שמואל אבוהב
bio: ר׳ שמואל בן אברהם אבוהב (1610–1694), known through his responsa דבר שמואל, was one of seventeenth-century Italy’s leading halakhic authorities. Born in Hamburg to a prominent Portuguese converso family, he was sent at thirteen to Venice to study under ר׳ דוד פרנקו, whose daughter he later married. He served for many years as rabbi of Verona, earning a reputation that drew students and questions from across Italy. In 1643 he organized assistance and ransom efforts for Jews of Kroměříž captured during the Thirty Years’ War, part of a lifelong commitment to communal charity and support for the Jews of ארץ ישראל. Called to Venice in 1650, he became av bet din and a central authority within the city’s cosmopolitan rabbinic world. During the Sabbatean crisis he opposed the movement and participated in the 1668 examination of נתן העזתי in Venice. His hundreds of responsa address ritual, communal and commercial problems across an extensive Mediterranean correspondence network. Near the age of eighty he temporarily left Venice under obscure circumstances, then returned before his death on 22 August 1694. His son ר׳ יעקב אבוהב published דבר שמואל in Venice in 1702 together with biographical and ethical material.
title: בעל דבר שמואל; אב בית דין ונציה

name: ר׳ ישראל יעקב בן שמואל חגיז
bio: ר׳ ישראל יעקב בן שמואל חגיז (1620–1674) was a Moroccan-born halakhist and educator who became a major builder of Jerusalem’s seventeenth-century scholarly world. Born in Fez, he travelled to Italy around 1646 to publish his writings and taught there for roughly a decade. With support from the Vega brothers of Livorno, he moved to Jerusalem around 1657 and established בית יעקב, a well-supported beit midrash and rabbinical academy. Its students included ר׳ משה בן חביב and ר׳ יוסף אלמושנינו, and its programme helped renew organised higher Torah study in the city. ר׳ ישראל יעקב was also a forceful opponent of Shabbetai Tzvi and his movement. His works combine pedagogy, halakhah and Mishnah study: תחילת חכמה and אורח מישור offered structured introductions to learning, while עץ החיים commented on the Mishnah. His responsa, הלכות קטנות, were published posthumously by his son ר׳ משה חגיז and became his best-known halakhic legacy. Around 1673 he travelled to Constantinople intending to publish further work and died there in 1674 before completing the project.
title: ראש ישיבת בית יעקב בירושלים

name: ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן
bio: ר׳ שבתי בן מאיר הכהן (1621–1662), הנודע כש״ך על שם ספרו שפתי כהן, היה מן הפוסקים החשובים במזרח אירופה במאה השבע־עשרה. הוא נולד באמשטיבובה שבליטא ההיסטורית — ויש מקורות המייחסים את לידתו לווילנה — ולמד אצל אביו ר׳ מאיר הכהן ובישיבות טיקטין, קרקוב ולובלין. לאחר נישואיו התיישב בווילנה והצטרף לבית דינו של ר׳ משה לימא. פירושו שפתי כהן ליורה דעה הופיע בקרקוב בשנים 1646–1647, כמעט במקביל לטורי זהב של ר׳ דוד הלוי סגל; שני החיבורים נעשו פירושי יסוד לשולחן ערוך. פלישת רוסיה לווילנה בשנת 1655 אילצה אותו לברוח מערבה. הוא עבר דרך לובלין ופראג, שימש ברבנות בשטרז׳ניצה, ולבסוף נתמנה לרב הולשוב במורביה, שבה נפטר בגיל צעיר. מגילת עיפה שלו היא עדות היסטורית־ספרותית לחורבן קהילות פולין וליטא בגזרות ת״ח–ת״ט. חיבוריו לחושן משפט וכתבים נוספים נדפסו בחלקם לאחר מותו. שנת פטירתו נמסרת לעיתים כ־1663 בשל המרת תאריכים, אך כ״א באדר א׳ תכ״ב תואם ל־1662 ונבחר כאן כשנת המפה.
title: בעל הש״ך; פוסק ורב בהולשוב

name: ר׳ משה זכות
bio: ר׳ משה בן מרדכי זכות (1625–1697), the הרמ״ז, was a central seventeenth-century kabbalist, poet, dramatist and communal rabbi. Born into a Portuguese New Christian family established in Amsterdam, he studied under ר׳ שאול לוי מורטירה and also acquired Latin and secular learning. Drawn intensely to mysticism, he pursued further Talmudic study in Poland. In 1644 he set out intending to reach the Land of Israel but remained in Italy, where he absorbed the Lurianic tradition associated with ר׳ בנימין הלוי. He settled in Venice, serving its community and participating in the editing and transmission of kabbalistic texts. In 1673 he accepted the rabbinate of Mantua, where he established an important circle for the study of Kabbalah; his leading disciples included ר׳ בנימין הכהן ויטאלי and ר׳ אברהם רוויגו. His correspondence connected Italian mystical circles and helped regulate the copying and interpretation of the writings of ר׳ יצחק לוריא. The הרמ״ז also wrote Hebrew poetry and drama: יסוד עולם is among the earliest substantial Hebrew dramatic poems, while תפתה ערוך depicts the punishments of Gehinnom. His halakhic and kabbalistic notes were collected as קול הרמ״ז, אגרות הרמ״ז and other posthumous editions. He died in Mantua on 1 October 1697.
title: הרמ״ז; מקובל ורב במנטובה

name: ר׳ מאיר בן יהודה לייב פאפירש
bio: ר׳ מאיר בן יהודה לייב פאפירש (c.1628–1662) was a Polish-born kabbalist whose editorial work shaped the European reception of Lurianic Kabbalah. Born into a prosperous Kraków family, he reached Jerusalem while young and studied in the circle of ר׳ יעקב צמח and other transmitters of ר׳ חיים ויטאל’s manuscripts. He became known not primarily for an independent mystical system but for arranging a difficult manuscript tradition into usable compilations. His recension divided Lurianic teaching into דרך עץ חיים, פרי עץ חיים and נוף עץ חיים; this arrangement became exceptionally influential in Poland and Germany and helped establish the textual form through which generations encountered the Ari’s teachings. Around 1649 he travelled back toward Poland carrying manuscripts, contributing directly to their circulation in Europe, before returning to Jerusalem. He also composed אור זרוע, a mystical alphabetic work, and other kabbalistic writings. He died young in Jerusalem in 1662. Conflicting older accounts of his birthplace and birth year are retained in the date note rather than presented as certainty.
title: מקובל ועורך כתבי האר״י

name: ר׳ אברהם אבלי הלוי גומבינר
bio: ר׳ אברהם אבלי הלוי גומבינר (c. 1637–1683), universally known as the מגן אברהם, was one of the most influential Polish halakhists of the seventeenth century. Born in Gombin, he lost his parents amid the upheavals associated with the Cossack massacres and continued his studies in Lithuania with his relative ר׳ יעקב יצחק גומבינר. He subsequently settled in Kalisz, where he served as a dayan and headed a yeshiva, apparently without holding the chief rabbinate. His great commentary on שולחן ערוך אורח חיים was originally called נר ישראל and was completed in an early form while he was still young. Revised in light of newly printed halakhic literature, it was published posthumously at Dyhernfurth in 1692 under the name מגן אברהם. Its compressed analysis mediates between the rulings of ר׳ יוסף קארו and ר׳ משה איסרליש, incorporates custom and kabbalistic practice, and became a central authority for Ashkenazic observance. His זית רענן on ילקוט שמעוני and a commentary on Tosefta Nezikin were also issued after his death. He died in Kalisz in poverty but with an enduring reputation as a foundational אחרון.
title: בעל מגן אברהם; דיין וראש ישיבה בקאליש

name: ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך
bio: ר׳ יאיר חיים בכרך (1638–1702), known as the חוות יאיר, was a major Ashkenazic halakhist, communal rabbi and polymath. Born in Lipník in Moravia into a distinguished rabbinic family, he moved as a child to Worms when his father ר׳ משה שמשון בכרך became its rabbi. He studied Torah alongside mathematics, astronomy and music, received rabbinic ordination, and served at Mainz and from 1666 at Koblenz. Returning to Worms in 1669, he taught and wrote but was passed over for the chief rabbinate after his father’s death. The French destruction of Worms in 1689 forced him and his family into a decade of displacement through Metz, Heidelberg and Frankfurt. When the community was reconstituted in 1699, he was finally appointed rabbi of Worms. That year he published חוות יאיר, 238 responsa named both for the biblical Havvot-Yair and in memory of his learned grandmother Chava. His rulings address ritual, civil law, communal governance, custom and early-modern technology. He also wrote מקור חיים on Orach Chaim, but withheld it after seeing the Taz and Magen Avraham; it appeared only in a modern edition. He died in Worms on 1 January 1702 and was buried in its Holy Sands cemetery.
title: בעל חוות יאיר; אב״ד וורמייזא

name: ר׳ שבתי משורר בס
bio: ר׳ שבתי בן ר׳ יוסף משורר בס (1641–1718), best known as the author of שפתי חכמים, was a biblical commentator, cantor, bibliographer and pioneering Hebrew printer. Born in Kalisz, he lost his parents in the persecutions of 1655 and fled to Prague. There he studied Talmud under ר׳ מאיר וֶרטֶרס, learned music from ר׳ לייב שיר השירים and sang bass in Prague’s Altneuschul; his vocal part produced the names Bass, Bassista and משורר. From 1674 to 1679 he visited Jewish scholarly centres and libraries across Poland, Germany and Holland. In Amsterdam he learned printing and proofreading and in 1680 issued שפתי חכמים, a concise guide to difficulties in רש״י’s Torah commentary, alongside שפתי ישנים, the first substantial bibliography of Hebrew books. After securing official permission, he established a Hebrew press at Dyhernfurth in 1689. The enterprise attracted Jewish workers and helped create a durable local community; his descendants continued it. A fire damaged the press in 1708. In 1712 Jesuit accusations led to his arrest and the confiscation of books, though he was ultimately acquitted. He later returned to Poland and died in Krotoszyn. His commentary remained widely printed beside רש״י, while שפתי ישנים made him a founder of Hebrew bibliography.
title: בעל שפתי חכמים

name: ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ
bio: ר׳ נפתלי בן יצחק הכהן כ״ץ (1648–1719), known as the סמיכת חכמים, was a prominent rabbi and kabbalist whose career connected Volhynia, Poland, Germany and the Ottoman world. Born in Ostroh to a distinguished rabbinic family, he was captured by Tatars as a youth and escaped after several years. He later succeeded his father in Ostroh and in 1690 became chief rabbi of Poznań. In 1704 he accepted the rabbinate of Frankfurt am Main. His major work סמיכת חכמים, printed in Frankfurt in two parts in 1704–06, developed connections among rabbinic texts and included his commentary on Berakhot. A devastating Frankfurt fire began in his home in 1711. Accusations that he had relied on practical Kabbalah rather than immediately combating the flames led to arrest and a trial; he was acquitted but left the city. He later spent time in Prague and Breslau and became involved in the controversy surrounding ר׳ נחמיה חייא חיון. Setting out toward the Land of Israel, he died in Constantinople in 1719. Later tradition remembers both his rabbinic authority and intense kabbalistic piety.
title: בעל סמיכת חכמים; אב״ד פוזנא ופרנקפורט

name: ר׳ דוד ניטו
bio: ר׳ דוד בן פנחס ניטו (1654–1728) was a Venetian-born physician, astronomer, philosopher and Haham of London's Spanish and Portuguese congregation. Educated in rabbinic learning and medicine, he practised and preached in Livorno, where he also pursued calendrical astronomy. Called to London in 1701, he became the first rabbinic leader to serve the congregation in the newly opened Bevis Marks Synagogue. His effort to explain divine providence through the language of ‘nature’ provoked accusations resembling Spinozism; ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי reviewed the dispute and vindicated his orthodox meaning. Nieto wrote in Hebrew, Spanish and Italian for a community containing former conversos who needed a reasoned defence of rabbinic tradition. מטה דן, also called the second Kuzari, defended the Oral Torah against Karaite and sceptical arguments and became his most enduring book. אש דת opposed Sabbateanism, while his Paschologia and communal calendars joined astronomy with practical religious calculation. He also answered Christian biblical polemic and served as physician alongside his communal office. He died in London in 1728 and was buried in the Velho cemetery at Mile End. His son ר׳ יצחק ניטו later held the Hahamship but is a separate person and record.
title: חכם קהל שער השמים בלונדון — בעל מטה דן

name: ר׳ יהודה בן שמואל רוזאניס
bio: ר׳ יהודה בן שמואל רוזאניס (1657–1727) was a leading Constantinopolitan halakhist, preacher and communal rabbi. He studied under ר׳ שלמה הלוי הזקן and ר׳ יוסף בן ישעיה מטראני, while initially supporting himself through the commercial house of his uncle and father-in-law ר׳ אברהם רוזאניס. He later devoted himself fully to scholarship and communal leadership in Constantinople. A determined opponent of lingering Sabbateanism, he participated in the campaign against ר׳ נחמיה חייא חיון, signing the ban against him in 1714 and later permitting a tightly conditional reconciliation. His best-known work, משנה למלך, is an extensive and enduring commentary on the Rambam’s משנה תורה, distinguished by its command of responsa and close analysis of earlier authorities. His sermons were published as פרשת דרכים, while דרך מצותיך treats the enumeration and classification of the commandments. His disciple ר׳ יעקב כולי edited and brought several of these writings to print after his death. Through משנה למלך in particular, ר׳ יהודה became a standard voice in the advanced study of the Rambam and later halakhic literature.
title: בעל משנה למלך; מחכמי קושטא

name: ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי
bio: ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי (1658–1718), הידוע כחכם צבי, היה פוסק נודד ומנהיג קהילות אשכנזיות וספרדיות. הוא נולד בטרביץ שבמורביה, גדל אצל סבו ר׳ אפרים הכהן בבודא ולמד בסלוניקי אצל ר׳ אליהו קובו; שליטתו במנהגי ספרד הקנתה לו את התואר חכם. לאחר טלטלות המלחמות העות׳מאניות כיהן בסרייבו, עבר לברלין, ולבסוף נעשה רב קהילות אה״ו. משנת 1710 הנהיג את הקהילה האשכנזית באמסטרדם והדפיס שם את שו״ת חכם צבי, ספרו המרכזי. הוא אישר את עמדתו האורתודוקסית של ר׳ דוד ניטו בוויכוח על טבע והשגחה, אך הסתכסך בחריפות עם הנהגת אמסטרדם סביב נחמיה חייא חיון וחשדות שבתאיים. בשנת 1714 עזב את העיר, שהה בלונדון ובקהילות גרמניה ופולין, וב־1718 נתמנה לרב לבוב ונפטר שם כעבור חודשים אחדים. בנו ותלמידו ר׳ יעקב עמדין המשיך את מאבקו בשבתאות והנציח פרטים מחייו. תאריך לידתו משתנה במקורות; שנת 1658 נבחרה משום שהיא מתאימה לתאריך העברי המפורט א׳ באלול תי״ח.
title: בעל שו״ת חכם צבי; רב אה״ו ואמסטרדם

name: ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה
bio: ר׳ חזקיה די סילוה (1659–1698), known as the פרי חדש, was a major Sephardic halakhist whose independent commentary became part of the standard שולחן ערוך page. Born in Livorno, he traveled around 1679 to Jerusalem and studied for a decade in the yeshiva of ר׳ משה גאלנטי. After his teacher’s death in 1689, he succeeded to leadership of the academy. As a Jerusalem emissary he traveled to Europe to raise funds and reached Amsterdam in 1691. Although offered a position in its Sephardic community, he declined and instead arranged publication of the first portion of פרי חדש on יורה דעה. The work subjects earlier rulings to close Talmudic review and does not hesitate to disagree with established authorities. Its unusually independent tone provoked opposition and a temporary ban in Cairo, yet later decisors widely accepted and cited it. Returning to Jerusalem, he continued teaching and writing and supported the side of ר׳ משה חגיז in a contemporary scholarly controversy. He died in Jerusalem in 1698 at only thirty-nine and was buried on the Mount of Olives. His son ר׳ דוד די סילוה continued the family’s literary legacy. Later editions expanded פרי חדש across additional sections of שולחן ערוך, ensuring his lasting influence on Sephardic halakhah.
title: בעל פרי חדש; ראש ישיבה בירושלים

name: ר׳ אהרן אורי פייבוש הארט
bio: ר׳ אהרן אורי פייבוש הארט (1670–1756) היה רבה הראשון של הקהילה האשכנזית המאורגנת בלונדון ונחשב בדיעבד למעין הרב הראשי האשכנזי הראשון של בריטניה. הוא נולד בברסלאו שבשלזיה, למד בישיבות בפולין ונשא את בתו של ר׳ שמואל בן אורי שרגא פייבוש, בעל בית שמואל. בראשית המאה השמונה־עשרה הגיע ללונדון והתמנה לרב בית הכנסת האשכנזי, לימים בית הכנסת הגדול בדוכס פלייס. סמכותו התרחבה מעבר לבירה כאשר קהילות מחוזיות צעירות פנו אליו בשאלות. מחלוקת חריפה סביב גט והחרמת מרקוס משה הובילה לפיצול שהתגבש כקהילת המבורו. להגנת פסיקתו פרסם בלונדון בשנת 1707 את אורים ותומים, החיבור הראשון שנדפס כולו בעברית בעיר. הוא המשיך לכהן עד מותו ב־1756. דיוקנו, שצייר ברתולומיו דנדרידג' ושחרט ג'יימס מקארדל בשנת 1751, נמצא באוסף הגלריה הלאומית לדיוקנאות ומספק תיעוד חזותי אותנטי בן זמנו. יש להבדילו מאחיו משה הארט, הנדבן שמימן את בניין בית הכנסת הגדול שנחנך ב־1722.
title: רב הקהילה האשכנזית בלונדון

name: ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק
bio: ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק (1680–1756), known from his classic Talmud commentary as the פני יהושע, was a major Polish-German rabbi of the early Acharonic period. Born in Kraków, he studied locally and after marriage settled in Lviv. A catastrophic gunpowder explosion in 1702 killed his mother, first wife and young daughter; rescued from the ruins, he vowed to devote himself to a work elucidating Talmud and Rashi, the project that became פני יהושע. After serving Tarlow, Kurow and Lesko, he became chief rabbi of Lviv in 1717/18. Communal conflict led to further appointments in Buchach, Berlin, Metz and, from 1741, Frankfurt am Main. His analytical novellae became a standard yeshiva text. He also intervened forcefully in public controversies, opposing ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ during the amulet dispute; the conflict contributed to his departure from Frankfurt in 1750. He subsequently stayed in Worms and Offenbach while retaining strong ties to Frankfurt. Parts of פני יהושע appeared in Amsterdam in 1739 and Frankfurt in 1752 and 1756; the final part appeared posthumously in Fürth in 1780. He died in Offenbach on 16 January 1756 and was buried in Frankfurt’s Battonnstraße Jewish cemetery.
title: בעל פני יהושע; רב לבוב, מץ ופרנקפורט

name: ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה
bio: ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה (בקירוב 1680–1765) היה מן החבורה המוקדמת של תלמידי ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב וממניחי היסוד להתיישבות החסידית בארץ ישראל. פרטי ראשית חייו אינם מתועדים היטב; שמו מעיד על זיקתו להורודנקה, והוא נזכר בין תלמידי החכמים שהתכנסו בברודי לפני שהתקרב אל ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב. במסורת החסידית תואר כאיש אמונו, כבעל תפילה וכמי שעסק בפדיון שבויים. בנו ר׳ שמחה נשא את פייגה, נכדת ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב; בנם היה ר׳ נחמן מברסלב. בשנת 1764 יצא לארץ ישראל בחבורה עם ר׳ מנחם מנדל מפרמישלן. הוא הגיע דרך נמל חיפה, שהה בצפת ולבסוף התיישב בטבריה. הוא נפטר בטבריה בב׳ בתמוז תקכ״ה, המזוהה עם 21 ביוני 1765, ונקבר בבית העלמין העתיק. מקורות אנציקלופדיים אחדים נותנים שנת פטירה מאוחרת יותר, אך התאריך המסורתי המפורט נבחר לציר הזמן. לא ידוע על ספר שחיבר בעצמו; אמרות בשמו נשמרו בספרות תלמידי ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב ובקבצים מאוחרים, ולכן אין לייחס לו חיבורים מודפסים כאילו פרסמם בחייו.
title: מתלמידי הבעל שם טוב

name: ר׳ יוסף בן עמנואל אירגאס
bio: ר׳ יוסף בן עמנואל אירגאס (1685–1730) was a Livornese rabbi, halakhist and kabbalist whose שומר אמונים became a classic systematic introduction to Lurianic Kabbalah. Born to Sarah and communal leader ר׳ עמנואל אירגאס, he studied Torah under ר׳ שמואל די פאס and spent an intensive period studying Kabbalah with ר׳ בנימין הכהן ויטאלי, a disciple of ר׳ משה זכות. After marrying Sarah in 1704, he lived for a time in Pisa, where he founded the Neveh Shalom yeshiva and charitable societies assisting poor brides and clothing the needy. Returning to Livorno, he became a communal rabbinic authority and answered questions from Italy and France. His leading student was ר׳ מלאכי הכהן, author of יד מלאכי. In 1710 he refused the Sabbatean propagandist ר׳ נחמיה חיון an approbation and drove him from Livorno; the resulting international pamphlet war produced תוכחת מגולה and הצד נחש in 1715. שומר אמונים, written as a dialogue, defends the authenticity and disciplined study of Kabbalah and became a leading statement that divine tzimtzum should not be understood literally. It was printed posthumously in Amsterdam in 1736, while דברי יוסף, sixty-eight responsa, appeared in Livorno in 1742. He died at only forty-five on 3 Sivan 5490. He must not be confused with the twentieth-century שומר אמונים of ר׳ אהרן ראטה.
title: בעל שומר אמונים הקדמון — רב ומקובל בליוורנו

name: ר׳ דוד אלטשולר
bio: ר׳ דוד אלטשולר (1687–1769), called the בעל המצודות, was an eighteenth-century rabbi and biblical commentator associated with Jaworów and Prague. He conceived a clear, accessible commentary on the Prophets and Writings that would gather the peshat explanations of earlier exegetes, especially ר׳ דוד קמחי, for readers unable to consult a large scholarly library. He served as rabbi in Jaworów and later in Prague. During his lifetime he completed or published portions on Psalms, Proverbs, and Job. His son ר׳ יחיאל הלל אלטשולר completed the wider project, edited and circulated it across Europe, and divided its material into two complementary commentaries: מצודת דוד, explaining the sense and flow of each verse, and מצודת ציון, defining individual words and expressions. This collaborative transmission explains conflicting summaries that attribute the final division either to father or son. Printed alongside the biblical text in innumerable editions, the מצודות became among the most widely read early-modern commentaries on נביאים and כתובים. No authenticated portrait is known.
title: בעל המצודות — פרשן הנביאים והכתובים

name: ר׳ נתנאל וייל
bio: ר׳ נתנאל בן ר׳ נפתלי צבי וייל (1687–1769), remembered as the בעל קרבן נתנאל, was a leading German-Bohemian Talmudist, rosh yeshiva and regional rabbi. Born in Stühlingen into a learned family descended from ר׳ יעקב וייל (מהרי״ו), he was orphaned young: his father and a brother were murdered in 1692. At ten he was taken to Fürth and then sent to Prague, where his uncle ר׳ ליפמן וייל raised him. He studied under ר׳ אברהם ברודא, who later arranged his marriage to a niece, פייגלא, in 1708. ר׳ נתנאל accompanied his teacher westward before returning to Prague in 1717. There he served as an assistant rabbi and prominent yeshiva teacher, reportedly educating a very large body of students. Maria Theresa’s expulsion of Prague’s Jews in 1744 forced another migration. In 1745 he became regional rabbi of the Black Forest communities, based at Mühringen, and in 1750 was appointed chief regional rabbi of the Baden-Baden and Baden-Durlach territories at Karlsruhe. He completed קרבן נתנאל there and published it in 1755—the first Hebrew book printed in Karlsruhe. Its precise textual and halakhic commentary on the rulings of ר׳ אשר בן יחיאל for the Talmudic orders מועד and נשים became standard in editions of the Talmud. He died during a visit to Rastatt and was buried in Karlsruhe. His son ר׳ ידידיה טיאה וייל succeeded him and helped preserve his writings.
title: בעל קרבן נתנאל
aliases: ר׳ נתנאל בן נפתלי צבי וייל

name: ר׳ יעקב כולי
bio: ר׳ יעקב כולי (c.1689–1732) was a Jerusalem-born scholar, editor and pioneering author in Judeo-Spanish. His maternal grandfather was ר׳ משה בן חביב, whose manuscripts he helped prepare for publication. After moving to Constantinople, he formed a close scholarly relationship with ר׳ יהודה רוזאניס and edited the latter’s משנה למלך and other posthumous writings. ר׳ יעקב’s lasting achievement was מעם לועז, begun in 1730 as an expansive Torah commentary in Ladino. It wove together biblical interpretation, halakhah, Midrash, ethics and practical religious instruction in language accessible to the broad Sephardic public. He completed Genesis and much of Exodus before his early death; later scholars continued the project across the remaining biblical books. The work became one of the foundational monuments of Judeo-Spanish religious literature and was subsequently translated into Hebrew and other languages. His editorial labours also preserved important works of both his grandfather and ר׳ יהודה רוזאניס. He died in Constantinople on 19 Av 5492, corresponding to 9 August 1732.
title: בעל מעם לועז; מחכמי קושטא

name: ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ
bio: ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ (1690–1764) היה מגדולי הפוסקים, הדרשנים וראשי הישיבות במרכז אירופה במאה השמונה־עשרה. הוא נולד לפי המסורת המקובלת באזור קרקוב, התייתם בצעירותו ולמד בפרוסניץ, בווינה ובפראג. בפראג הנהיג ישיבה, דרש ברבים, עסק בהיתר הדפסת התלמוד תחת הצנזורה הנוצרית, וב־1736 התמנה לדיין. ב־1741 עבר למץ ושימש כרב העיר וכראש ישיבה. בשנת 1750 נבחר לרב שלוש קהילות אה״ו—אלטונה, המבורג וונדסבק—אחד המרכזים החשובים של יהדות אשכנז. זמן קצר לאחר בואו פרצה מחלוקת הקמעות: ר׳ יעקב עמדין טען כי נוסחי קמעות שכתב מעידים על זיקה שבתאית. ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ דחה את ההאשמות, והמחלוקת פילגה קהילות והעסיקה בתי דין ושלטונות במשך שנים; המחקר המודרני ממשיך לדון במסמכים. שיעוריו וחידושיו נעשו יסודיים בלימוד ההלכה. כרתי ופלתי על יורה דעה ואורים ותומים על חושן משפט הם מחיבוריו המרכזיים, ויערות דבש משמר את דרשותיו. רוב כתביו נדפסו לאחר מותו בידי תלמידים ובני משפחה. הוא נפטר באלטונה בשנת 1764 ונקבר בבית העלמין היהודי שם.
title: רב פראג, מץ וקהילות אה״ו

name: ר׳ אריה לייב גינצבורג
bio: ר׳ אריה לייב בן ר׳ אשר גינצבורג (c. 1695–23 June 1785), conventionally known from his responsa as the Sha’agat Aryeh, was an eighteenth-century Lithuanian Talmudist, halakhic authority and rosh yeshivah. Born in Pinsk, he assisted his father after the latter became rabbi of the Minsk district and in 1733 established a major yeshivah in Minsk. His teaching there generated conflict with ר׳ יחיאל היילפרין over methods of Talmud study; although he used pilpul pedagogically, the introduction to שאגת אריה criticizes pilpul when it obscures legal truth. After leaving Minsk, he became rabbi of Volozhin in 1750 and taught students including ר׳ חיים מוולוז׳ין and ר׳ רפאל זיסקינד הכהן. שאגת אריה, prepared in Volozhin and first printed in 1755, established his enduring reputation through closely argued discussions of laws chiefly in Orach Chaim. After a period of travel he was called to Metz in 1765; royal confirmation followed in 1766. He remained its rabbi, av bet din and head of yeshivah until his death. His later טורי אבן and posthumous גבורת ארי extended his critical, source-driven analysis across several Talmudic tractates and became staples of advanced yeshivah study.
title: בעל שאגת אריה; אב״ד ור״מ מץ

name: ר׳ חיים בן עטר (אור החיים הקדוש)
bio: ר׳ חיים בן משה בן עטר (1696–1743), universally known from his Torah commentary as the אור החיים הקדוש, was a Moroccan Sephardi Torah commentator, halakhist, Talmudist, preacher and kabbalist. Born in Salé, he learned first from his grandfather and namesake ר׳ חיים בן עטר הזקן. Political insecurity took the family to Meknes during his childhood, after which he taught in Salé and later Fez. Economic pressure, famine and his aspiration to establish a major academy in the Land of Israel shaped his departure from Morocco. After passing through Algiers, he built a circle of patrons and students in Livorno, arranged publication of his writings in Amsterdam and Venice, and sailed with his wives and roughly thirty disciples to Acre in 1741. Epidemics delayed entry into Jerusalem, so the group spent about a year in the Galilee before settling there in 1742. In Jerusalem he founded מדרש כנסת ישראל, with divisions for advanced revealed Torah and kabbalistic study; ר׳ חיים יוסף דוד אזולאי was among the scholars associated with his academy. He died after less than a year in Jerusalem and was buried on the Mount of Olives. His אור החיים combines close textual interpretation, halakhic reasoning, homily and kabbalistic theology and became especially influential across Sephardi, North African and Hasidic communities. Miraculous stories and an intended meeting with ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב belong to later devotional tradition and are not treated here as independently documented travel.
title: אור החיים הקדוש

name: ר׳ יעקב ישראל עמדין
bio: ר׳ יעקב ישראל בן צבי אשכנזי עמדין (1697–1776), known by the acronym יעב״ץ, was a North German halakhist, critic, printer and one of the most forceful opponents of crypto-Sabbateanism. Born in Altona, he was educated chiefly by his father ר׳ צבי הירש אשכנזי, the חכם צבי, and followed the family through Amsterdam and central Europe. After marriage he lived in Brody and studied in the celebrated kloyz. His only sustained communal rabbinate was at Emden from 1728 to 1733, from which his surname derives. Returning to Altona, he chose relative independence, earning through commerce and a private Hebrew press established in the 1740s. This enabled him to publish responsa, liturgy, textual criticism, grammar, Kabbalah and polemic without ordinary communal controls. His שאלת יעב״ץ and מור וקציעה remain important halakhic works; his siddur combines text, law and commentary, while מטפחת ספרים applies unusually critical analysis to the Zoharic corpus. From 1751 his accusation that amulets of ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ contained Sabbatean formulas generated an international rabbinic controversy, bringing bans, civil intervention and intense personal attacks. His autobiographical מגילת ספר is an exceptional, candid source for eighteenth-century rabbinic family and communal life, though also a partisan self-defence. He died in Altona in 1776 and was buried in its Königstraße Jewish cemetery.
title: היעב״ץ — פוסק, מדפיס ולוחם בשבתאות

name: ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב
bio: ר׳ ישראל בן אליעזר בעל שם טוב (traditionally 1698–1760), known as the Baal Shem Tov or Besht, was a healer, religious mystic and charismatic leader in Polish Podolia, regarded as the founder of modern Hasidism. Tradition locates his birth at Okopy, but nearly all accounts of his childhood and early adulthood come from later Hasidic hagiography; contemporary evidence becomes substantial only during his mature career. He worked in Podolian towns, reportedly as a teacher, ritual slaughterer and circumciser, learned rabbinic literature and practical and contemplative Kabbalah, and became known during the 1730s as a baal shem—one who healed and mediated spiritual or personal difficulties. His wife Chana was the sister of ר׳ אברהם גרשון מקיטוב; their children were Tzvi Hirsh and Udl, whose descendants became important Hasidic leaders. In 1740 he settled at Medzhybizh, where estate records document a tax-exempt communal house and identify its occupant successively as a kabbalist, baal shem and “baal shem doctor.” He led a circle of scholarly mystics that included ר׳ יעקב יוסף מפולנאה, ר׳ דב בער ממזריטש, ר׳ פנחס מקוריץ and ר׳ נחמן מהורודנקה. His teachings emphasized divine presence throughout existence, prayer with attachment and intention, joy, humility and service through ordinary material life. He authored no systematic book. His sayings survive chiefly through students’ writings, later anthologies and a small, textually disputed body of letters. He died and was buried in Medzhybizh in 1760; his disciples transformed his circle into a durable movement after his death.
base_name: Yisrael ben Eliezer, the Baal Shem Tov
title: הבעל שם טוב — מייסד החסידות

name: ר׳ מלאכי בן יעקב הכהן
bio: ר׳ מלאכי בן יעקב הכהן (c. 1700–1772), commonly known as the יד מלאכי, was an Italian Talmudist, halakhic methodologist and kabbalist. Born and educated in Livorno, he became a leading disciple of the kabbalist ר׳ יוסף אירגאס and later succeeded him in a local rabbinic role. His responsa circulated among Italian scholars and appear in collections of contemporaries, including תודת שלמים of ר׳ ישעיהו באסאן. A ruling dated 1732 shows his participation in an Italian legal network, though it does not establish residence in Rome. During the controversy surrounding ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ and ר׳ יעקב עמדין, the Livorno rabbinate signed in support of ר׳ יהונתן אייבשיץ. His major work, יד מלאכי, first printed in Livorno in 1766–1767, systematizes rules governing Talmudic terminology, the methods and relative authority of codifiers, and principles used in responsa and legal decision-making. Its exhaustive citations made it one of the most durable works of rabbinic methodology. He also composed שבחי תודה for a Livorno communal fast in 1744 and wrote a Torah scroll renowned locally for its scribal forms. He died in 1772; the precise place and day are not securely documented, and the map therefore retains Livorno as his last evidenced centre rather than asserting a precise burial site.
title: בעל יד מלאכי; מחכמי ליוורנו

name: ר׳ יהודה בן שמעון אשכנזי
bio: ר׳ יהודה בן ר׳ שמעון אשכנזי (c.1700–1743), often called the Baal Be’er Heitev, was a German-born Polish dayan and halakhic compiler. Born in Frankfurt am Main to a family in which his father served as scribe and communal officer, he later settled in Tykocin and served on its rabbinical court. His באר היטב condensed decisions of earlier and contemporary authorities and responsa into brief annotations accompanying Shulchan Aruch. Editions appeared in Amsterdam during his lifetime, including Yoreh De’ah in 1736, Even HaEzer in 1739 and Orach Chaim in 1742. In the standard composite באר היטב now printed with Shulchan Aruch, his annotations are retained chiefly for Orach Chaim and Even HaEzer. The Yoreh De’ah and Choshen Mishpat portions commonly printed under the same title are by a different scholar, ר׳ זכריה מנדל בן אריה ליב of Belz; another earlier work with the same title was written by ר׳ ישעיה בן אברהם הלוי. Distinguishing these authors is essential: באר היטב is a shared title and later editorial composite, not evidence that one person wrote every present section.
title: בעל באר היטב; דיין בטיקטין
aliases: Judah ben Simon Sofer Frankfurt Ashkenazi

name: ר׳ יצחק ניטו
bio: ר׳ יצחק ניטו (1702–1774) היה חכם ספרדי־פורטוגלי בלונדון, מתרגם תפילות ורבה הראשון של הקהילה היהודית המאורגנת בגיברלטר. הוא היה בנו של ר׳ דוד ניטו, חכם קהל שער השמים בבית הכנסת בוויס מרקס. לאחר מות אביו התמנה ר׳ יצחק ניטו בשנת 1733 לחכם הקהילה בלונדון. הוא פרש מן התפקיד ב־1741 ושהה מחוץ לאנגליה; כשחזר ב־1747 עסק גם כנוטריון. בשנת 1749 יצא לגיברלטר, שם הנהיג את הקהילה וקשור לייסוד קהל שער השמים—בית הכנסת הגדול והעתיק של המושבה. ב־1751 שב ללונדון לפי בקשת הקהילה והתמנה אב בית דין לצד ר׳ יצחק דה ואלה ור׳ יעקב קורונל. מחלוקת פנימית על סמכויות ותארים בבית הדין הביאה להתפטרותו במרץ 1757 ולהפסקת כהונתו ביולי. לצד עבודתו הרבנית פרסם תרגומים ספרדיים חשובים למחזורי ראש השנה ויום הכיפורים ולסידור ימות החול, וכן דרשה מוסרית דו־לשונית בעת יום צום מלכותי ב־1756. תרגומיו השפיעו על נוסחי תפילה ספרדיים מאוחרים. הוא נפטר בלונדון בשנת 1774. יש להבדילו מאביו ר׳ דוד ניטו, שלו רשומה נפרדת בפרויקט.
title: חכם קהל שער השמים בלונדון ורבה הראשון של גיברלטר

name: ר׳ דוב בער ממזריטש
bio: ר׳ דוב בער בן אברהם (c.1704–15 December 1772), the Maggid of Mezeritch, was the principal organizer and systematic teacher of the second generation of Hasidism. Born at Lokachi in Volhynia, he received advanced rabbinic education traditionally associated with ר׳ יעקב יהושע פאלק, author of פני יהושע. Before entering the Hasidic circle he lived as an ascetic kabbalist and served as a preacher in Volhynian communities including Turchyn, Korets and Rivne. In the mid-eighteenth century he became a disciple of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב at Medzhybizh; the encounter redirected his spirituality from bodily mortification toward divine immanence, joy and devekut. After the Baal Shem Tov's death in 1760, most of the emerging movement's leadership gathered around the Maggid at Mezhirichi. His relatively stationary court trained and dispatched a network of disciples—including ר׳ מנחם מנדל מוויטבסק, ר׳ שניאור זלמן מלאדי, ר׳ לוי יצחק מברדיטשוב, ר׳ אלימלך מליז׳נסק and ר׳ אהרן הגדול מקרלין—who spread Hasidism across Eastern Europe. The Maggid wrote no systematic book; students edited oral teachings into מגיד דבריו ליעקב and related collections. He moved to Hannopil during a 1772 epidemic, died there on 19 Kislev 5533 and was buried in its Jewish cemetery.
base_name: Dov Ber ben Avraham, the Maggid of Mezeritch
title: המגיד ממזריטש — המגיד הגדול

name: ר׳ מאיר מרגליות
bio: ר׳ מאיר מרגליות (c.1707–1790), known as the מהר״ם מרגליות and בעל מאיר נתיבים, was a major Galician–Podolian halakhist and one of the early rabbinic adherents of ר׳ ישראל בעל שם טוב. Born into the distinguished Margolies family, he studied within the learned networks of Volhynia and Galicia and encountered the Besht before Hasidism became a mass movement. He held rabbinic and judicial positions in several communities, including Horodenka and Lviv, and eventually became rabbi of Ostroh. A royal appointment of 1775 designated him rabbi of Bratslav and a wider Ukrainian district within the Polish Commonwealth, reflecting his recognized legal authority. His responsa מאיר נתיבים address ritual, civil and communal law and preserve correspondence with leading contemporaries; the first edition was printed posthumously at Polonne in 1791–92. Other works include אור עולם, דרך הטוב והישר and the kabbalistic סוד יכין ובועז. His relation to early Hasidism did not displace his conventional role as dayan and regional authority; rather, later traditions remember him as connecting elite rabbinic jurisprudence with the Besht's circle. He died in Ostroh on 10 Iyar 5550 and was buried near ר׳ שמואל אליעזר הלוי איידלס. The prior project claim that he emigrated to New York and served Shearith Israel was wholly false and has been removed.
title: המהר״ם מרגליות — בעל מאיר נתיבים

name: ר׳ משה חיים לוצאטו
bio: ר׳ משה חיים לוצאטו (1707–1746), הרמח״ל, היה מקובל, הוגה, משורר ומחזאי עברי. הוא נולד בגטו פדובה למשפחה אמידה, קיבל חינוך תורני וכללי ולמד אצל ר׳ ישעיהו באסאן. כבר כנער חיבר שירה, מחזות וספרי לשון. סביב 1727 הודיע כי מגיד שמימי מוסר לו גילויים, והקים חוג קבלי. על רקע הטראומה השבתאית עוררו טענותיו התנגדות חריפה מצד ר׳ משה חגיז ורבני ונציה ופרנקפורט. הוא התחייב להגביל את כתיבתו הקבלית, וחלק מכתביו נגנזו או נשרפו. בשנת 1735 עבר לאמסטרדם, התפרנס כלוטש יהלומים והמשיך לכתוב ללא הנהגת חוג מיסטי פומבי. שם פרסם את מסילת ישרים בשנת 1740, שעתיד להיות מספרי המוסר המרכזיים, וכן חיבורים בשיטת התלמוד, אמונה, השגחה ורטוריקה. דרך ה׳ ודעת תבונות מציגים באופן שיטתי את מחשבתו הקבלית. בשנת 1743 עלה עם משפחתו לעכו. ב־1746 נספו הוא ובני ביתו במגפה. מסורת קבורתו בטבריה נפוצה, אך מקום הקבורה ההיסטורי שנוי במחלוקת. כתביו השפיעו עמוקות על הקבלה, תנועת המוסר והספרות העברית החדשה.
title: הרמח״ל; בעל מסילת ישרים

name: ר׳ חיים שמואל יעקב פאלק
bio: ר׳ חיים שמואל יעקב פאלק (1708–1782), the בעל שם מלונדון, was an itinerant kabbalist, healer, alchemist and practitioner of divine-name traditions who became one of eighteenth-century Anglo-Jewry's most enigmatic figures. His origins are uncertain: sources place his birth either in Fürth or Pidhaytsi.
